objections.claim: The sole credential-bearing merge controller is not protected by any stated external trust anchor. `VERIFIER_CLOSURE_DIGEST` covers the gate closure and `TRUSTED_WORKFLOW_DIGEST` covers `.github/workflows/`, while the signed transition tuple and `covered_files` omit `workflows/tools/merge-controller.mjs` and its closure. A controller-only PR can therefore pass the existing controller's eligibility checks, merge, and replace the future sole merger with code that skips every safeguard. Protect and base-source the controller's complete closure under an out-of-tree digest, require an Eye-signed transition for changes, and add a controller-only bypass fixture. Candidate sha256:7c71ee8498b005fbdf79392c8f1b2e7c3885786d56c0fb33bf5da0df7c0609ba.

Production authority still depends on mutable check names: readiness contracts permit `check_names[]`, E1 accepts required checks as merely green, and release asserts a required-CI check run at the tag SHA without binding its producer or workflow bytes. GitHub's Checks API permits multiple same-name runs and exposes `app_id` separately, so an untrusted producer can publish a green same-name run at the exact SHA and satisfy these mechanisms. This violates the frozen prohibition on authority from mutable names. Bind check evidence to authenticated producer plus immutable workflow/configuration identity and exact run provenance, and add a same-name/untrusted-app collision fixture that must fail. Candidate sha256:7c71ee8498b005fbdf79392c8f1b2e7c3885786d56c0fb33bf5da0df7c0609ba.
